data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE:
#   The PBS job name uses a positional parameter ($1): `#PBS -N GPM_$1`.
#   Flux batch directives must be static (no shell expansion), so the job name
#   cannot be parameterized portably here.
#
# Run with:
#   flux batch <this_script> -- <partition_id>

# PBS resources:
#   -A GT-rbras6-CODA20
#   -l nodes=1:ppn=15
#   -l mem=20gb
#   -l walltime=00:30:00
#   -j oe

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 15
#flux: --time-limit=30m

# Omitted PBS option: -A GT-rbras6-CODA20 (account)
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS option: -l mem=20gb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -j oe (join stdout/stderr)
# Flux commonly manages stdout/stderr separately; a portable join directive is not guaranteed.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but logs may be split.

# Omitted PBS option: parameterized job name (GPM_$1)
# Flux batch directives are static; no portable way to inject $1 into --job-name.
# Performance implication: none, but job identification in the queue may be less informative.

PARTITION_ID=$1
if [ -z "$PARTITION_ID" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <partition_id>" >&2
  exit 2
fi

/bin/echo Running on host: "$(hostname)".
/bin/echo In directory: "$(pwd)"
/bin/echo Starting on: "$(date)"

# Activate environment
source activate ~/venvs/pydask

/bin/echo Parition "$PARTITION_ID"

python /storage/coda1/p-rbras6/0/njadidoleslam3/projects/stochsm/model_simulations/postprocess/create_unified_data.py "$PARTITION_ID"

reasons: PBS requested 20gb of memory (`-l mem=20gb`) but the Flux resource section includes no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
